classification.difficultyReason: Requires considering all three positions of the given angle and both valid ambiguous-case triangles.

content.prompt: Find all possible areas of a triangle with two sides of length $10$ and $11$, and one angle of $60^\circ$, correct to two decimal places.

inlines.text: Consider the included angle and the angle opposite each given side; use both valid sine-rule solutions.

answer.worked:
Let $K$ be the area. The $60^\circ$ angle can lie between the given sides or opposite either given side.

If it is the included angle:
$$\begin{align*}K&=\frac12(10)(11)\sin60^\circ\\K&\approx47.63\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$

If it is opposite the side of length $10$, let $B$ be opposite the side of length $11$:
$$\begin{align*}\sin B&=\frac{11\sin60^\circ}{10}\\B&=\alpha\text{ or }180^\circ-\alpha,\qquad \alpha=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{11\sin60^\circ}{10}\right).\end{align*}$$
Both choices give a positive third angle. The included angle is $120^\circ-\alpha$ or $\alpha-60^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}K&=55\sin(120^\circ-\alpha)\approx40.68\text{ units}^2\\K&=55\sin(\alpha-60^\circ)\approx11.71\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$

If it is opposite the side of length $11$, let $B$ be opposite the side of length $10$:
$$\begin{align*}\sin B&=\frac{10\sin60^\circ}{11}\\B&=\beta,\qquad\beta=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{10\sin60^\circ}{11}\right).\end{align*}$$
Here $\beta<60^\circ$, so the supplementary choice would make the angle sum exceed $180^\circ$. Thus:
$$\begin{align*}K&=55\sin(120^\circ-\beta)\\K&\approx51.02\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$

The possible areas are $11.71$, $40.68$, $47.63$ and $51.02\text{ units}^2$. All calculations use unrounded angles.
